title: Information Satisfaction: A Reader-Centered Axis for Summarization Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2608.14457v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The majority of work on summarization evaluation focuses on general summary quality (e.g., ROUGE, BERTScore) or specific desired properties (e.g., readability, factuality). However, these metrics fail to measure the utility of a summary to an individual user. For example, a biomedical researcher learning about the latest vaccine research will have different informational needs from a family doctor. Query-focused summarization captures part of this need, but in practice, users rarely state everything relevant in a query: a single short query is likely inadequate to distinguish the needs of a researcher from those of a physician. translated_title: 信息满意度：以读者为中心的摘要评估轴心
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.14457v1 公告类型：新 摘要：大多数关于摘要评估的工作集中在一般摘要质量（如ROUGE、BERTScore）或特定期望属性（如可读性、事实性）上。然而，这些指标无法衡量摘要对单个用户的实用性。例如，一位了解最新疫苗研究的生物医学研究者与一位家庭医生的信息需求不同。查询聚焦摘要捕捉了这一需求的一部分，但在实践中，用户很少在查询中陈述所有相关内容：一个简短的查询可能不足以区分研究者与医生的需求。相比之下，读者的背景或个人特征（其角色和专业知识）在查询间相对稳定，并恢复了大部分缺失的上下文，这使其成为评估摘要是否满足该读者需求的实际信号。在这项工作中，我们评估了流行摘要指标对这些因素的敏感程度。
tldr: 本文提出以读者背景（角色和专业知识）为中心的信息满意度作为摘要评估的新轴心，弥补现有指标忽略个体需求的不足。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes reader-centered information satisfaction based on background and expertise as a new axis for summarization evaluation, addressing the gap in existing metrics that overlook individual user needs.
